A driver admission in the chat_log is one of the independent corroborating sources named in POL-RD-07, and it is matched by his formal counterparty statement that he 'took a wrong turn at the MCE exit and had to come back around'.

The gps_trace is clean and needs no corroboration: 229 fixes over 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and a 10 s sampling interval well inside the 30 s ceiling. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes and the deviation may be established on it alone.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-04 does not apply: nothing in the chat_log is a rider instruction to detour. The three messages are the rider querying the route and the driver apologising, and every message carries waypoint_hint null, so the clause is unavailable on this record and exonerates nothing.

POL-RD-05 does not apply: the trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. There was no relocated endpoint, so the booked optimal of 21.0 km governs unchanged.

POL-RD-12 does not apply: the vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. There is no matched pooled itinerary to subtract, so the 21.0 km solo optimal stands as the correct baseline.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip identifier TRP-00101 matches across the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The rider_profile records deviation_claims_60d of 0, so the extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not triggered. I cite that profile counter only for the POL-RD-08 test it names, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, which applies because fare_model is METERED. charged_total is 35.64; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63; refund = 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 8.05. The rider's own recollection of 'around $27' is very close to the recomputed 27.63, which is the fare he should have paid. At 22.5% of charged_total the refund is far below the 90% full-refund share and well above the 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

POL-RD-09 adds no separate line here and creates no double count: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP and toll charges (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0) and no airport surcharge, so the pass-through correction has nothing to bite on and the POL-RD-02 refund stands as the whole of the money the rider is owed.

The rider's own threshold case caps out below materiality. The governing trace distance under POL-RD-01 is 27.18 km against a 21.0 km optimal route — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.43% — which passes the establishment gate (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) but is below both materiality markers of 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute. This is therefore a non-material deviation: no FULL_REFUND of charged_total and no repeat-driver uplift of the kind POL-RD-06 licenses can be awarded on this record.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to uplift anything. The driver's trailing-90-day deviation counter reads 0 against 812 completed trips — a ratio of 0.0, far below the 0.05 ratio and the count of 3 that POL-RD-06 sets as the pattern test. With no pattern established, the remedy stays at the POL-RD-02 figure and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is warranted either.

The rider asks for a $10.00 difference; POL-RD-02 fixes the sum lower. On this METERED fare the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63, against a charged_total of 35.64, giving a refund of 8.01 — 8.05 once rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05. At 22.5% of the charge it is far below the 90% full-refund share, and above the 0.50 de minimis. A PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05 is the very most the record allows.

Nothing may be added on the pass-through side. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines at all — erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and off-route ERP is 0.00 — and POL-RD-09(1) forbids stacking off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 amount in any event. The driver's monetary exposure ends at the 8.05 refund, with no separate surcharge or gantry correction on top.

The driver does not dispute the missed MCE exit — he says so in his own chat message — so this is not a case about whether the route went wrong. Nor is any exoneration route open on this record: the rider gave no detour instruction the driver could act on (POL-RD-04), the traffic-advisory artifact is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no closure or external cause can be asserted, and no pickup or dropoff endpoint was amended. Decided on the arithmetic alone, the rider recovers 8.05 and not a cent more.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the route did go wrong, and the money follows the arithmetic rather than either party's recollection of it.

The deviation is established under POL-RD-01. The governing figure is the GPS trace distance of 27.18 km (EV-GPS-00101), not the trip record's rounded 27.2 km, which POL-RD-01 says may not be cited for the threshold test. Against the 21.0 km optimal route that is an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.43% — passing both establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%). It is below the materiality markers (50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute), so this is a non-material deviation: no FULL_REFUND of the charge and no POL-RD-06 uplift. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (EV-GPS-00101: 229 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s sampling, all inside POL-RD-07(a)–(c)), so it alone carries the finding; the driver's chat message 'sorry boss missed the exit' (EV-CHAT-00101) and his formal statement that he took a wrong turn at the MCE exit confirm the cause independently in any event.

No exculpatory clause applies. There was no rider detour instruction (POL-RD-04 — every chat waypoint_hint is null, so nothing to act on), no endpoint amendment (POL-RD-05 — all amendment fields null), no pooled itinerary (POL-RD-12 — vehicle_type RYDE_X, solo optimal null), no upfront quote (fare_model is METERED), and no traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 can excuse no part of the excess.

The refund is fixed by POL-RD-02. charged_total is 35.64; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63; refund = 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 8.05. That is 22.5% of the charge — far below the 90% full-refund share and well above the 0.50 de minimis. The rider claimed a 10.00 difference; the record allows 8.05, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top: the fare breakdown carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), so there is no pass-through correction and no double count. Driver compensation under POL-RD-04 does not arise — the rider was billed 27.2 km, slightly MORE than the 27.18 km driven, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall. The driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 812 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is warranted; there is no phantom charge line, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral either. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires.

Confidence is capped at 1.0 and set at 0.95: every artifact carrying a deciding fact — EV-GPS-00101, EV-TRIP-00101, EV-FARE-00101 and EV-CHAT-00101 — carries weight 1.0, and the one impaired artifact in the pool (EV-ADVIS-00101-01, weight 0.0) is not relied on for any finding.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
